chunks: Abu 'Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from Abi Ibrahim عليه السلام, who said:
The hand of the thief is cut, and his thumb and the palm of his hand are left; and his foot is cut, and his heel is left so that he may walk on it.

key_terms.إِبْهَامُهُ: his thumb, which is left intact
key_terms.السَّارِقِ: the thief, the person guilty of theft
key_terms.رِجْلُهُ: his foot, referring here to the limb subject to cutting
key_terms.صَدْرُ رَاحَتِهِ: the inner palm of his hand, which is left intact
key_terms.عَقِبُهُ: his heel, which is left so he can walk
key_terms.يَدُ: the hand, referring here to the limb subject to cutting

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about how the hadd punishment for theft is carried out?
ai.summary: This hadith states the legal ruling concerning the prescribed bodily punishment for theft, specifying the parts to be cut and the parts to be left intact. It reflects the precision of fiqh in defining the limits of the hadd punishment while preserving minimal bodily function.
